title: Philippine Coast Guard adds 3 vessels into service
summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Wednesday has commissioned three vessels into service as part of efforts to bolster operational capabilities in protecting the country's maritime territories.

blocks.text: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Wednesday has commissioned three vessels into service as part of efforts to bolster operational capabilities in protecting the country's maritime territories.

“The newly commissioned vessels will expand our conduct of maritime safety operations and responses to emergencies at sea, including oil spills and other incidents that threaten the country's rich marine environment,” PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said in a statement.
The commissioning of the three vessels was held at the National Headquarters in Port Area, Manila led by PCG Commandant Admiral Rommel Supangan.
Two of the vessels, namely the BRP Patag (PATS-2701) and BRP Pag-asa (PATS-2702), are 27-meter marine protector-class patrol boats.
The boats came from the United States and were acquired after 24 PCG crew members completed specialized training in Baltimore, Maryland last August.
The third vessel is the BRP Kalikasan (MRSV-2001), a 20-meter marine research and survey vessel which will be used for shallow-water hydrographic surveys and ocean conservation.

The PCG said the BRP Kalikasan was built locally in Cebu as part of the PCG’s long-term capability expansion project. It was already used in a mission in Corregidor Island early this month. — BAP, GMA News
